title: Claude Code Desktop Redesign — Multi-Session Sidebar & Integrated Terminal
description: Anthropic shipped a complete redesign of the Claude Code desktop experience on April 14, 2026 (v2.1.108). Key features: (1) Session sidebar for managing multiple parallel Claude Code sessions from a single window — replaces cmd-tabbing between terminal tabs. (2) Drag-and-drop workspace layout for arranging session panels. (3) Integrated terminal pane within the Claude Code UI. (4) Faster diff viewer for reviewing file changes. (5) Expanded preview area. This is a client-side UX upgrade — no API key required, works on Max plan. Distinct from Routines (cloud automation) and Agent Teams (parallel programmatic agents). Primary value: visibility into parallel sessions without external tooling like tmux or the community 'Claude Control' macOS app (HN #47765520).
notes: Released same day as Routines (April 14). MacRumors, SiliconAngle, and MikeGingerich.com all confirmed. Primarily relevant for Mac/Windows desktop app users. On requiem (native Linux CLI workflow), tmux handles parallel session management equivalently — direct impact is limited unless the Linux desktop app ships with same features.

evaluation.reasoning: Official Anthropic release (community_validation=100), zero integration needed — it's an automatic app update (complexity=100), Anthropic-maintained (maintenance=100). Token efficiency is neutral — pure UX change, no effect on context consumption. Capability expansion (35): meaningful for Mac/Windows desktop app users managing parallel sessions; limited for our Linux/tmux CLI workflow on requiem where the desktop app is not the primary interface. Our tmux session management achieves equivalent parallel-session visibility natively. Integration action: registry entry only — add to existing-capabilities.md as a documented official feature under a 'Desktop App' section. No configuration changes required.
